描述_ZN: Scroll of Landscape in Green and Blue, Ming dynasty, painted by Dong Qichang, on silk with color, 117 cm in length and 46.1 cm in width.　　This scroll is inscribed in running script with three self-titled inscriptions.　　The upper right inscription reads: "Painting with a water brush dipped in ink, also a small variation of ink splashing. Inscribed by Xuanzai on the second day before Tanabata in the autumn of Dingwei." Inscription at the bottom: "Seal of Dong Qichang". The first seal is "Painting Zen". Ding Wei was painted in 1607, the 35th year of the Ming Dynasty, the year Dong was 53 years old, the year after he resigned from his studies in Huguang, while he was living idly in the village.　　The top left is inscribed with a seven-word poem "The Fisherman" by Liu Zongyuan: "The fisherman is staying at the west rock at night, and at dawn he draws the bamboo from the clear river. The smoke disappears at sunrise and no one is seen, and the mountain and water are green with a sound of Hey Nai. Looking back at the sky and the middle stream, there is no (human) heart on the rock and the clouds are chasing each other. Dong Xuanzai." (For the original poem, see Quan Tang Poems, vol. 353.) Inscriptions below: "Tai Shi Shi" and "Dong Qichang".　　The inscription in the middle of the left part reads: "When Shih suppressed his brother, he hated that he did not get more of Yu's paintings. This picture is hidden by the son and Lu Junze, who appreciated it and wanted to take it away. Yu said when gun more benefit less, and make Shi suppression can boast of Jun Ce. Jun Ce since the work of painting, and nothing, this cloth teaching also. Xinhai spring is the second day Dong Xuanzai." Xinhai was the thirty-ninth year of the Wanli era (1611), when Dong Qichang was living idly in the village.　　The collection seals include "Ke Ting Appreciation", "Cai Collection", and "Ancient She Hong Yi Men Appreciation Seal".　　This picture is also known as "Xi Yan Xiao Ji Tu". The picture is left virtual and right real, half of the wall with s-shaped composition painting the cliff huge towering, giving people a sense of novelty. There are several trees under the cliff, the lake is silent, the reeds are dotted with small boats, and the pines and cypresses on the cliff are clustered. The picture is drawn with stone green and stone green, the reeds and fishing boats are outlined with fine strokes, and the leaves of the trees are painted with the boneless method, which is rich in variations of intensity and lightness. The mountains and rocks are chapped and rubbed with the brush, highlighting the strange peaks. The ink is pale and moist, and the work is quiet and serene, a masterpiece of Dong's mid-career.
